title: Mary close: do whatever he tells you
hookLine: every Marian title points back to her son

cards: A wedding in Cana, a village in Galilee, and the party is going well, until the wine runs out. For the bride and groom, this is a disaster in front of everyone they know. The guests haven't noticed yet.
The steward hasn't noticed. One guest has. Mary goes to her son and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "They have no wine."
He answers with something that sounds like a gentle refusal. She doesn't argue. She turns to the servants instead, and what she tells them closes these days on Mary.

teach.b: You heard this story in year one; today, watch Mary. First, she notices. Nobody asked her to watch the wine.

She sees a need in somebody else's house and carries it straight to her son. That's the picture Catholics have when they ask her to pray for them: someone who notices what's running out, and takes it to him.
Second, she steps aside. Her words to the servants, in the Douay-Rheims: "Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye."

teach.h: DO WHAT HE SAYS, NOT WHAT I SAY.
teach.b: Not do what I say: do what he says. Then she's out of the story. The servants fill the stone jars with water, carry some to the steward, and it's wine, the good wine, saved for last.

Some readers notice that John's Gospel gives her no more lines after this; if so, her last words in it are an instruction to listen to someone else. Third, every title. Mother of God, because of who her son is.
Ever virgin, a life kept for him. Conceived without sin, by his grace. The new Eve beside the new Adam.
Queen, because he is king. Taken up, because he rose first. The tilma, where she carries him.
Lourdes and Fatima, where the message is pray. The Catechism puts it in one line: what Catholics believe about Mary rests on what they believe about Christ.
Every name points past her. Fourth, what comes next.

teach.h: NEXT, THE CHURCHES OF THE EAST.
teach.b: Tomorrow the path turns east, to the churches that pray in Greek, Arabic, Syriac and Slavonic and still stand with Rome.

teach.h: WHATSOEVER HE SHALL SAY TO YOU, DO YE.
teach.b: Mary comes along, under the name the East gives her: Theotokos, the one who bore God.

how: Catholics read the wedding at Cana in the Mass and pray it as a Luminous Mystery of the rosary, and Catholic writers quote Mary's words to the servants when they explain devotion to her.

games.q: you're Mary at the wedding. the wine has run out, and your son's first answer sounds like no. what do you do?
o: argue with him in front of the guests.
tell the servants to do whatever he says.
go and find more wine yourself.
games.why: she turns to the servants: "whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye." then she steps out of the story, and the water becomes wine.

practice: Choose one thing Jesus asks in the Gospels that you already know, forgive, love your neighbor, give to the one who asks, and let it get small and concrete: one person, one action.
If you pray, bring it to Mary the way the wedding did and hear her line again, whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye; if not, simply hold the one thing.

wordCard.voice: Mary close. The end of the days on Mary, at a wedding in Cana, where the mother sends everyone to her son. Today's word.
